To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Intermediary Design Delivers (IDDs) are representations of the evolving shared exhibition- idea that mediate the boundary crossing across museum designer teams.
the digital exhibition design is a process of boundary crossing that is mediated by IDDs, which embody past processes of consent and mediate future ones.

digital exhibition design is a collaborative process that involves a number of different stakeholders, and the use of Intermediary Deliverables (IDDs) is crucial for facilitating collaboration between these stakeholders and for mediating the design space of the digital exhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and role that digital exhibition design deliverables play in the design process.
the role of design deliverables in digital exhibition design and the implications this has for the museum team’s role.
the role of design deliverables in the digital exhibition design space and the implications for museum teams and designers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IDDs mediate the boundary crossing of the museum team and the digital exhibition designer team, and that IDDs are a means to facilitate the production of the digital exhibition by embodying past processes and future possibilities.
IDDs are representations of an evolving exhibition-idea that mediate boundary crossing and facilitate processes of consent.
IDDs are boundary objects that mediate the boundary crossing across museum teams and digital designers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the digital exhibition design is an iterative and progressive process of exploration of the exhibition-idea.
the IDDs mediate a boundary crossing process that is a key to understanding the nature and role that digital deliverables play in the production of digital exhibitions.
IDDs are boundary crossing and progressive objectification devices that mediate future and embody past processes of consent in the digital exhibition design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the digital exhibition design space is a social space, in which the design team is a key participant.
IDDs are not only a means to an end, but also a medium for the evolution of the digital exhibition idea.
the digital exhibition design team needs to be aware of and sensitive to the nature of the IDDs that are produced.
